notes.title: How to attempt Seen Passages
notes.content:
1. Read the activities first, then the passage.
2. **A1/B1 (Simple Factual - 2 marks):** Objective type (True/False, Fill in the blanks, Match columns, Complete the web). Answers are directly in the passage.
3. **A2/B2 (Complex Factual - 2 marks):** Information transfer, Wh- questions. Answers found in different parts of the passage.
4. **A3/B3 (Vocabulary - 2 marks):** Meanings, opposites, word forms.
5. **A4/B4 (Contextual Grammar - 2 marks):** Tenses, voice, narration based on the passage.
6. **A5/B5 (Personal Response - 2 marks):** Your opinion/views on an issue arising from the passage.

notes.title: Lesson 1.2 The Thief's Story - A1. Complete the following
notes.content: (i) The 'I' in the story refers to the narrator, who called himself Hari Singh. (ii) Anil kept Hari as a cook because he wanted someone to cook for him. He perhaps also felt sorry for Hari.

notes.title: Lesson 2.5 Let's March - B1. True or False
notes.content:
(i) Kailash Satyarthi sees children growing freely with dignity. -> True
(ii) Let us march from morality to divinity. -> False

notes.title: Lesson 2.5 Let's March - B2. Complete the given diagram: Children's Rights
notes.content: Right to life, right to freedom, right to health, right to education, right to safety, right to dignity, right to equality, and right to peace.

flashcards.front: What are the qualities of Anil in 'The Thief's Story'?

quiz.question: In 'The Thief's Story', why did Anil keep Hari as a cook?
options: Because Hari was an excellent chef
Because Anil wanted someone to cook and felt sorry for him
Because Anil needed a partner for his business
quiz.explanation: Anil wanted someone to cook for him and perhaps also felt sorry for Hari.
